summary: Hundreds of surfers, both amateur and professional, are gathering on California's West Coast to ride massive waves generated by a powerful storm in the Pacific Ocean, which is producing one of the largest tidal waves in recent years.

head: Cambiamento climatico: “La Svizzera deve finalmente agire”
summary: The European Court of Human Rights has condemned Switzerland for its insufficient measures to protect its citizens from climate change, prompting the country to re-evaluate its climate policies and consider stronger measures to meet its climate goals.

head: Schengen compie 40 anni
summary: The Schengen area, which includes Switzerland and allows for free movement of people between 29 European countries, is facing new tensions and internal controls 40 years after its establishment, with some member states reintroducing border controls due to the pandemic and migration concerns.

head: Senza una tregua, a Gaza si continua a combattere
summary: Fighting continues in Gaza as Israeli tanks reach the city of Khan Yunis, with over 18,000 Palestinians reported dead, and the United Nations agency for Palestinian refugees accusing Israel of attempting to forcibly relocate the Strip's two million inhabitants.

head: Amherd respinge le critiche di Mosca
summary: Swiss President Viola Amherd has rejected Russian criticism of Switzerland's involvement in a potential global summit on peace in Ukraine, stating that Switzerland has always stood on the side of international humanitarian law.

head: Mendrisio, prima pietra per il nuovo liceo e apertura nel 2028
summary: A new high school in Mendrisio, Switzerland is under construction and expected to be completed by 2028, with a total investment of 48 million francs. The project includes the construction of five levels, as well as additional buildings and infrastructure for the local population, and is part of a larger educational complex that will be completed by 2038.

head: Ecco che cos’è l’ICE
summary: The Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agency in the US is a federal agency responsible for enforcing immigration laws, with powers to arrest and detain individuals suspected of being in the country illegally. ICE agents, often wearing tactical gear and masks, conduct operations in public and private spaces, sparking controversy over their role, tactics, and use of force, with critics arguing that the agency's actions create a climate of fear and make it difficult to hold individuals accountable.

head: Bimbi di Gaza verranno curati in Svizzera
summary: The Swiss government has decided to accept and provide medical care to a group of injured children and their families from the Gaza Strip, with the operation expected to involve around 20 victims of Israeli attacks.

head: “The Pitt”, “Adolescence” e “The Studio” trionfano agli Emmy
summary: The Emmy Awards ceremony saw several notable wins, including "The Studio" for best actor and direction, "Adolescence" for best direction, writing, and supporting actor and actress, and "The Pitt" for best drama series, while "Severance" and "The White Lotus" were also nominated in various categories.

head: Il voto a 16 anni non convince
summary: A proposal to lower the voting age to 16 in Riehen, Switzerland has been rejected by the local population and a majority of users on the online platform "dialogo", with many arguing that 16 and 17-year-olds lack the maturity and life experience necessary to make informed political decisions.

head: UNRWA: “Inchiesta su violazioni stabili ONU”
summary: The head of the UN agency for Palestinian refugees (UNRWA), Philippe Lazzarini, is calling for an independent investigation into alleged UNRWA building violations in Gaza, in response to Israeli accusations of a Hamas tunnel beneath the agency's headquarters.

head: Tribunale federale, lascia il presidente Yves Donzallaz
summary: Swiss Federal Tribunal President Yves Donzallaz will step down at the end of the year after one term, citing a desire to give space to new forces and allowing a new person to lead the institution with fresh enthusiasm, particularly as it approaches its 150th anniversary in 2025.

head: Gaza, la Berlinale attaccata dal “suo” sindaco
summary: At the Berlin International Film Festival, several filmmakers, including Ben Russell and Basel Adra, publicly accused Israel of genocide during a ceremony, citing the deaths of nearly 30,000 people in Gaza, mostly civilians. This led to a controversy, with the mayor of Berlin, Kai Wegner, accusing the filmmakers of anti-Semitism, while others defended their right to free expression.

head: Affitti in rialzo: la crisi degli alloggi accende il confronto politico
summary: The housing market in Switzerland continues to experience a significant increase in rents, with a 0.4% rise in February 2026, driven by a shortage of apartments, particularly in major cities like Zurich, where prices have risen by over 50% since 2009.

head: Iniziativa vaccini “superata e imprevedibile”
summary: A Swiss initiative aimed at protecting individual freedom and physical integrity, known as the "vaccination initiative," has been deemed "superfluous and unpredictable" by critics, who argue that its objectives are already guaranteed by the federal constitution and that its vague language raises concerns about potential consequences for state actions.

head: Iniziative sanità, parte la campagna del comitato favorevole
summary: A coalition of politicians from the Centre and PS parties has launched a campaign to address rising healthcare costs in Switzerland, proposing two initiatives: "For a brake on costs" and "For less burdensome premiums," which aim to limit the increase in healthcare costs to 20% above the growth of salaries and the economy, and to cap premiums at 10% of disposable income, respectively.

head: Quando ballare poteva essere pericoloso anche in Ticino
summary: A recent incident in Crans-Montana, Switzerland has highlighted concerns about safety measures in public venues, particularly nightclubs, which are often overcrowded and located in underground areas, posing potential fire risks if adequate safety measures are not implemented.

head: Piazza federale, l’allarme scattò per uno zaino sospetto
summary: A 48-year-old Italian man with mental health issues was found guilty of "public intimidation" after an incident on October 18, 2023, at the Federal Square in Bern, Switzerland, where a suspicious backpack led to a two-hour evacuation, although it was later found to contain a harmless wooden box and a cable.

head: Trump sembra “imbattibile”. Ma perché?
L’opposizione russa in piazza a Berlino
summary: Russian dissidents and opposition leaders gathered in Berlin for a major protest against the invasion of Ukraine and the regime of Vladimir Putin, marking the first time the opposition has taken to the streets in large numbers to demonstrate against the Russian government and the conflict in Ukraine.

head: Iniziative sanità, parte la campagna del comitato favorevole
summary: A coalition of politicians from the Centre and PS parties has launched a campaign to address rising healthcare costs in Switzerland, proposing two initiatives: "For a brake on costs" and "For less burdensome premiums," which aim to limit the increase in healthcare costs to 20% of the growth in salaries and economy, and to cap premiums at 10% of disposable income, respectively.

head: La pianificazione ospedaliera “resti ai Cantoni”
summary: The Swiss cantonal health directors' conference opposes centralizing hospital planning authority to the federal government, arguing that the cantons are better equipped to address regional healthcare needs and should maintain control over planning, while also promoting cooperation and coordination.

head: Il Covid, in versione “Frankenstein”, non fa paura
summary: The new variant of the SARS-CoV-2 virus, dubbed "Frankenstein," is more contagious than previous versions but not more dangerous, with experts noting that hospitals are not overwhelmed and current vaccines remain effective against it.

head: Lumino, avviso di acqua non potabile
summary: Due areas in the town of Lumino, specifically Via Bellinzona, Via alla Torre, and part of Via Castione, have been declared non-potable due to possible microbiological contamination, requiring residents to boil the water for at least 5 minutes before consumption.

head: Attentato di Mosca, spunta una pista turca
summary: Russian investigators are exploring a new lead in the Moscow attack, suggesting that two of the four attackers spent time in Turkey before the bombing, and may have received funding from a Turkish source, while the Russian government continues to accuse Ukraine of involvement in the attack.

head: Mori, dalla fuga di notizie al dialogo che non c’è
summary: A controversy in Mendrisio, Switzerland, surrounding the traditional "Mori" (black-faced) figures in Easter processions has led to a reversal of a decision to stop painting the figures' faces black, with the issue to be revisited after the processions.

head: Germania: alle origini del successo dell’AfD
summary: The Alternative for Germany (AfD) party has achieved its highest national vote share of 20.8% in the February 2025 elections, becoming a major force in German politics. The party's success is not limited to the eastern regions, but is now a national phenomenon, with a strong presence in both eastern and western Germany, driven by a growing electorate that votes for the party out of conviction rather than protest.

head: Oggi niente scuola, ma il Liceo di Bellinzona resta aperto
summary: The Liceo di Bellinzona in Switzerland is open today, January 7, despite a scheduled school closure, as students and teachers participate in a protest against a decision to compensate a missed salary increase with additional vacation days.

head: Consiglio federale: norme “too big to fail” da rafforzare
summary: The Swiss Federal Council has approved a package of measures to strengthen the "too big to fail" regulations following the Credit Suisse crisis, aiming to reduce risks for the economy, state, and taxpayers by improving bank governance, increasing liquidity, and developing crisis management tools.

head: A 12 anni in una cella israeliana: “È stata una tortura”
summary: Palestinian minors, including a 14-year-old boy named Seif and a 12-year-old boy named Mohammad, have been arrested and detained by Israeli authorities, often on arbitrary charges, with many experiencing harsh conditions and torture in prison.

head: Svizzeri più aperti verso la NATO
summary: A recent survey conducted by the Politecnico di Zurigo found that 82% of Swiss citizens view the global situation with pessimism, but a majority also believe that the country's military is necessary and that increasing collaboration with NATO is desirable, with 52% in favor of increased cooperation.

head: Parsi, “Trump ascolta solo Israele”
summary: Italian professor Vittorio Emanuele Parsi argues that the US administration under Trump is ignoring the concerns of Arab allies and the European Union, prioritizing Israel's interests, and that this approach may lead to a lesson for Iran that "those with nuclear capabilities stay in power, while those without risk falling."

head: Libano, la guerra lungo i fili del telefono
summary: The Christian village of Rmeich in Lebanon is resisting the presence of Hezbollah fighters, who have installed their telephone network in the area, as the villagers fear being attacked by Israel and are seeking a safe zone to avoid being caught in the crossfire.

head: Migranti e respingimenti, Jans avverte Berlino
summary: Swiss Federal Councilor Beat Jans has criticized Germany's new asylum policy, which allows for the rejection of asylum seekers at the border, and has hinted at possible countermeasures, stating that Switzerland's measures are stronger than they appear.

head: Evasione dal carcere Beccaria a Milano, in tre in fuga
summary: Three teenage boys, including two brothers, escaped from the Beccaria juvenile prison in Milan on Sunday, the latest incident in a series of breakouts and disturbances at the facility, which has struggled with overcrowding and staffing issues.

head: Ponte Brolla, un cantiere tra stazione ed esasperazione
summary: Residents in Ponte Brolla, Switzerland have been experiencing noise and dust pollution from a construction site for over a year, with the demolition of a rock wall expected to be completed by the end of the month and the site to be closed by the end of the year.

head: Rinforzi russi nella regione di Kursk
summary: Russian forces have been deployed in the Kursk region, where a special regime has been introduced due to a Ukrainian military incursion, with Moscow's defense ministry reporting the loss of 945 Ukrainian soldiers and dozens of vehicles in four days.

head: “Tutti gli ostaggi liberi o distruggeremo Gaza City”
Un alunno su sei è sovrappeso
summary: According to a Swiss health foundation's monitoring, approximately one in six schoolchildren in Switzerland are overweight or obese, a rate that has slightly decreased to 16.7% in the 2022/23 school year.

head: Il destino degli svizzeri partiti per unirsi all’IS
summary: A Swiss citizen, identified as Fabien, has been detained in a Syrian prison for eight years without a trial for his alleged involvement with the Islamic State. He hopes for a change in government in Damascus, which could influence his situation, and is seeking repatriation to Switzerland, despite the country's current stance of not accepting the repatriation of its citizens who joined the Islamic State.

head: Le pietre della memoria di Brissago
summary: For the first time in Ticino, four memorial stones were placed to remember the deported Jewish members of a family who were turned away at the border, highlighting a dramatic story of courage and solidarity among the people of Brissago.

head: Piante e insetti traviati da un gennaio primaverile
summary: Un inverno primaverile anomalo in Svizzera sta causando problemi per le piante e gli insetti, con temperature elevate che rischiano di danneggiare i germogli delle piante e di far uscire gli insetti troppo presto dalla loro dormienza invernale, rendendo difficile la loro sopravvivenza.

head: Netanyahu: “Israele continuerà a colpire l’Iran con tutta la sua forza”
Formazione e ricerca: 29,2 miliardi per il 2025-2028
summary: The Swiss federal government has decided to allocate 29.2 billion Swiss francs for education and research from 2025 to 2028, with the aim of promoting long-term education, research, and innovation.

head: Sunak stringe sul piano Ruanda, “pronti i primi voli”
summary: British Prime Minister Rishi Sunak has launched a decisive push to implement the controversial "Rwanda Plan," which aims to relocate asylum seekers who have arrived illegally in the UK to Rwanda. Sunak has stated that the plan will proceed "come what may," with the first flights to Kigali expected to depart within 10-12 weeks.

head: Grigioni, un cold case da riaprire?
summary: A recent investigation suggests that far-right extremists may have intentionally set an arson fire in 1989 that killed four Tamil people, including two young brothers, at a refugee center in Chur, Switzerland, prompting a local politician to request a re-examination of the case.

head: Gli stretti rapporti tra la Svizzera e il dalai lama
summary: The Dalai Lama, the spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhists, is visiting Switzerland for the 16th time, but the country's official relations with the Tibetan community have cooled down in recent years, coinciding with an increase in economic ties with China.

head: La SSR prevede un ritorno alle FM
summary: The Swiss Broadcasting Corporation (SSR) plans to resume broadcasting on FM radio after the Swiss Parliament approved a delay in the transition to digital-only broadcasts, citing a change in the political and public expectations regarding the use of FM technology.

head: Rinviato il dibattito sulle donne afghane
summary: A debate in the Swiss National Council about granting asylum status to Afghan women living in Switzerland has been postponed due to a lack of time for further discussion, with the issue expected to be revisited on Wednesday.

head: Tagli della Confederazione, anche le città insorgono
summary: The Swiss Union of Cities criticizes the federal government's budget-cutting plan, which would impose 6.3 billion francs in cuts by 2028, and argues that the plan unfairly burdens urban populations with service cuts and increased responsibilities.

head: Gaza City, “stiamo estendendo le operazioni”
summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has announced an escalation of military operations in Gaza City, with the goal of taking control of the city, which is considered a stronghold of Hamas, and destroying infrastructure and buildings used for terrorism.

head: Il controverso svizzero che consiglia la flottiglia per Gaza
summary: Anouar Gharbi, a Swiss citizen of Tunisian origin and president of the "Centre genevois pour la démocratie et les droits humains," has been accused of having ties to Hamas, a Palestinian Islamist organization, due to his involvement with various organizations that have supported Hamas in the past. Despite these allegations, Gharbi claims to have no direct contact with Hamas representatives since 2023 and has been providing consultancy services to the "Waves of Freedom Switzerland" association, which is organizing a flotilla to Gaza.

head: Grigioni: 7 luoghi d’arte da conoscere
summary: The Grigioni region in Switzerland is home to a variety of unexpected art spaces, including converted barns, historic buildings, and old cellars repurposed as galleries, showcasing local and international artists' works in a unique and immersive experience.

head: Gli USA non vogliono un’escalation in Medio Oriente
ONU, il voto su Gaza rinviato ancora
summary: The United Nations Security Council vote on the Gaza situation has been postponed again to Wednesday to allow for further negotiations on the draft resolution, which calls for a "suspension" of hostilities to facilitate the delivery of more humanitarian aid.

head: Berna, l’analisi della situazione col capo dell’UNRWA
summary: The Swiss head of the UNRWA, Philippe Lazzarini, is invited to a meeting with the Swiss government's foreign policy commission to discuss the agency's situation following allegations of ties to Hamas and the suspension of funding by several countries.

head: Maltempo Brasile, oltre cento morti e danni ingenti
summary: Over 100 people have been killed and nearly 1.5 million affected by severe floods in the Brazilian state of Rio Grande do Sul, with estimated reconstruction costs totaling approximately 3.4 billion francs.

head: Limitare il traffico in Città Vecchia a Locarno fa discutere
summary: The Municipality of Locarno is proposing a 3-month experiment to limit traffic in the historic city center, which would involve closing or restricting access to certain streets, but the local business owners are strongly opposed to the idea, citing concerns about the impact on their livelihoods and the city's commerce.

head: Partecipare alla democrazia, sfida per la Quinta Svizzera
summary: The Swiss diaspora, comprising over 813,400 citizens living abroad, is growing and seeking greater participation in Swiss democracy, including electronic voting and increased support from the government, to strengthen their ties with the country.

head: Agente dell’ICE spara di nuovo a Minneapolis
summary: A US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent shot a Venezuelan citizen in Minneapolis, sparking calls from local authorities for the agent to leave the city and state, amid ongoing tensions and criticism of federal government actions.

head: Abolizione del valore locativo, le stranezze di un voto
summary: The Swiss population's vote on abolishing the locative value, a tax on homeowners, has raised questions about the outcome, with a majority of voters approving the measure in most cantons, despite it benefiting a minority of homeowners, and being rejected in cantons where homeowners are in the majority.

head: Soldi ai migranti? Solo in forma prepagata
summary: The Swiss UDC party is proposing the introduction of a prepaid debit card for asylum seekers, inspired by a similar project in Germany, to make the country less attractive to migrants and improve financial control, but the proposal is met with opposition from the government and humanitarian organizations.

head: Quando i gesti parlano, “ma non è sempre stato così”
summary: The lives of deaf people in Switzerland have undergone significant changes, with advancements in technology, education, and language accessibility, but challenges persist, particularly in recognizing the official status of sign languages and ensuring equal participation in public life.

head: I senza religione sono sempre più numerosi
summary: According to updated statistics from the Swiss Federal Statistical Office, people without a religious affiliation have become the largest group in Switzerland, making up 35.6% of the population, surpassing Catholics and significantly decreasing the number of Evangelical Reformed Protestants.

head: Allenaza commerciale tra Pechino, Seul e Tokyo
summary: In response to the US trade offensive led by President Trump, China, Japan, and South Korea have announced plans to strengthen their cooperation to create a predictable business environment, stabilize supply chains, and improve communication on export controls.

head: Nasce il “carrello sospeso” per i bisognosi
summary: A Swiss startup called WeSherpa has developed a digital platform that allows donors to leave a "credit" at local stores, which can be redeemed by people in need, giving them the freedom to choose essential items such as food, medicine, and services.

head: Amherd a Parigi fra sport e diplomazia
summary: Swiss President Viola Amherd is in Paris for the 2024 Olympic Games, where she will support the country's athletes and also attend the "Paris Summit 2024" on sports and sustainability, with a focus on Switzerland's potential bid to host the 2038 Winter Olympics.

head: Trump minaccia di ricorrere all’Insurrection Act
summary: US President Donald Trump has intensified pressure on the state of Illinois and the city of Chicago, threatening to invoke the Insurrection Act to override local opposition and court decisions against deploying National Guard troops.

head: Risarciti gli asilanti imprigionati illegamente
summary: The Swiss Federal Tribunal has ruled in favor of two asylum seekers who were detained illegally after their asylum requests were rejected, and the government must now compensate them for their wrongful imprisonment.

head: Aumenta la tensione tra India e Pakistan
summary: Tensions between India and Pakistan are escalating, with Pakistan warning that any Indian attempt to increase tensions after a recent incident in the disputed region of Jammu and Kashmir would meet a "very strong" response, while also condemning India's decision to suspend a water treaty as "illegal and highly irresponsible".

head: Viola Amherd lascia il Consiglio federale
summary: Swiss politician Viola Amherd has announced her resignation from the Federal Council, effective at the end of March, after serving for six years and 30 years in active politics.

head: Gaza: il massacro che ha spezzato il sogno occidentale
summary: Egyptian-Canadian author and journalist Omar El Akkad expresses his loss of faith in Western values due to the ongoing Israeli attack on Gaza, which he believes has resulted in a genocide. He criticizes the hypocrisy of Western leaders and institutions for their silence on the issue, and argues that the use of violence, boycotts, or narrative resistance against colonialism and capitalism is met with various forms of suppression.

head: “C’è speranza”: cosa pensano gli ucraini dei negoziati
summary: Most Ukrainians support negotiations to end the conflict, with over half of the population favoring a quick resolution through talks with the US and Europe, bringing hope for a swift end to the war.

head: UE, ecco la squadra del von der Leyen bis
summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has unveiled her new team of commissioners, with a focus on competitiveness, climate, and security, and a 40% female representation, but critics argue that economic priorities may overshadow climate ambitions ahead of European elections.

head: Gaza, le armi tacciono
“Responsabilità ambientale” verso la bocciatura
summary: A recent survey in Switzerland indicates a strong opposition to an initiative aimed at promoting environmental responsibility, with 61% of respondents opposing the measure, which seeks to limit the country's consumption of resources and emissions of harmful substances in line with global environmental limits.

head: Surses e gli altri no, offensiva solare a rischio?
summary: The town of Surses in Switzerland has rejected a large solar power project, citing concerns about the impact on the natural environment and local tourism, which may jeopardize the country's "Solarexpress" initiative to increase winter energy production.

head: Votazioni in Svizzera: tra riforme fiscali, energia e mobilità
summary: Citizens in various Swiss cantons voted on key issues such as taxation, energy transition, transportation, and territorial planning, with notable results including the rejection of a proposal to reduce corporate tax rates in Zurich and the approval of a revision to the energy law to accelerate the construction of wind and renewable energy facilities.

head: “Un giorno va bene per una patente di pesca”
summary: The newly appointed president of the Swiss Federal Commission for Migration, Manuele Bertoli, has expressed concerns about a proposed 24-hour asylum procedure for migrants from North Africa, suggesting it may lead to summary procedures.

head: Mandato di arresto per Schoigu e Gerassimov
summary: The International Criminal Court has issued arrest warrants for Russian former Defense Minister Sergei Shoigu and Chief of General Staff Valery Gerasimov for alleged war crimes related to the invasion of Ukraine, specifically the deliberate destruction of electrical infrastructure and civilian casualties.

head: Riccio, dove sei?
summary: The European hedgehog population is declining in Switzerland, with a 40% drop in the last 25 years, prompting the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) to classify the species as "potentially threatened" globally. A participatory science campaign, "Riccio, dove sei?", aims to census the hedgehog's presence in southern Switzerland, with over 400 sightings reported in the first seven months, highlighting the need for conservation efforts and public awareness to protect the species.

head: Salmone dal colore “acceso”? Dipende dal krill
summary: The krill, a small crustaceo in Antarctic waters, is a crucial component of the ecosystem, providing food for various marine animals, including whales, seals, penguins, and seabirds. However, its population has declined by nearly 80% since the 1980s due to overfishing, driven by the demand for krill-based products such as omega-3 supplements, fish feed, and farmed salmon. Experts warn that the krill's decline has significant implications for the entire Antarctic ecosystem, including increased climate instability and the risk of its collapse.

head: Esercitazione contro la peste suina africana
summary: Swiss authorities conducted an exercise in the Mendrisiotto region to prepare for the potential arrival of the African swine fever virus, which is lethal to pigs and wild boars but harmless to humans, by testing drones and teams to detect infected animals and safely disposing of carcasses to prevent the spread of the disease.

head: Terza notte di disordini in Nuova Caledonia
summary: Violent protests have erupted in New Caledonia, a French territory in the Pacific, following the approval of a constitutional reform by the French National Assembly that could weaken the indigenous Kanak minority, resulting in two deaths and hundreds of injuries.

head: Custodire la Terra, non dominarla
summary: The Catholic Church is reevaluating its stance on the relationship between humans and the natural world, shifting from a focus on dominating nature to a sense of responsibility and stewardship, as exemplified by Pope Francis's encyclical Laudato si' and the recent introduction of a Mass for the Custody of Creation. This change is driven by growing environmental crises and a recognition of the interconnectedness of all living beings, echoing the ideas of Saint Francis of Assisi and classical philosophers who saw the natural world as a sacred and interconnected whole.

head: Francesco, da domani l’omaggio dei fedeli
Trump bis: tra decreti esecutivi e le sentenze dei giudici, l’America già cambia
summary: In the first seven months of his second presidency, Donald Trump has issued a record number of executive orders, with over 200 orders signed, and has been involved in nearly 400 legal cases, with many decisions being appealed or blocked by the courts, creating confusion and uncertainty about the legality of his actions and the effectiveness of his presidency.

head: Ticino a mano armata, un Far West di soldi morti e rapine
summary: In the 1970s and 1980s, the Swiss-Italian region of Ticino experienced a surge in armed robberies, with banks, post offices, and other businesses being targeted by increasingly brazen criminals. The situation escalated to the point where a bank employee was killed in 1977, and the region became a hub for illicit activities, with the local police struggling to keep pace. The robberies continued to worsen, with the use of violence and intimidation becoming more common, and the introduction of new security measures only seeming to drive the perpetrators to more extreme actions, including the use of hostage-taking and the seizure of valuable items.

head: UE e mandato negoziale: secondo avallo dal Parlamento
summary: The Swiss parliament's committee on foreign affairs has approved the country's negotiating mandate with the EU, with 9 votes in favor, 3 against, and one abstention, despite some criticisms regarding the proposed dispute resolution system and other aspects of the agreement.

head: “… e la Svizzera tace”
summary: A Swiss professor of international law, Evelyn Schmid, expresses concern that Switzerland's official statements on the Gaza situation are too vague and do not go far enough in addressing the humanitarian crisis, particularly in light of Israel's new foundation for controlling aid distribution, which she considers a problematic development.

head: Riforma fiscale, reclamo del PS: “Errore grossolano nell’opuscolo”
summary: The co-president of the Italian Socialist Party, Laura Riget, has criticized the government for an "obvious error" in an informational pamphlet about a tax reform vote, which she claims is part of a series of misleading information, and has requested the government to correct the mistake and provide accurate information to the public.

head: La Croce Rossa Sottoceneri annuncia 35 licenziamenti
summary: The Swiss Red Cross Sottoceneri Section has announced 35 layoffs as part of a cost-cutting measure in the Area Migrazione, which will affect 30.5 full-time positions.

head: A Gaza la tregua sembra ancora lontana
summary: As the Ramadan month approaches, a Gaza ceasefire seems increasingly unlikely, with the conflict entering its sixth month and a death toll of nearly 31,000, while a potential second front in Lebanon is also emerging.

head: AfD al bando? I pro e i contro
summary: Germany is divided over the possibility of banning the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party, which has gained significant support with over one-fifth of the electorate, after a secret meeting revealed plans to deport millions of immigrants, sparking widespread protests and calls for the party's ban.

head: Si decarbonizza, ma spalmando i 100 milioni su più tempo
summary: The Swiss parliament, the Gran Consiglio, has approved a package of subsidies worth 100 million francs to support private companies transitioning from fossil fuels to renewable energy, with the incentives to be spread over 9 years instead of the initially proposed 5 years.

head: Il valore del volontariato: storie di impegno silenzioso in Ticino
summary: The value of volunteering is highlighted through the stories of two women, Nadja and Maria, who dedicate their time to helping others in their community in Ticino, Switzerland, demonstrating the transformative power of volunteering and its importance in bringing people together and promoting personal growth.

head: Francia in piazza contro razzismo ed estrema destra
summary: Tens of thousands of people in France gathered in cities across the country on Saturday to protest against racism, the rise of far-right politics, and the government's immigration policies, with some demonstrators also targeting US President Trump and his advisor Elon Musk.

head: Vaud, presa d’ostaggi: l’assalitore è stato ucciso
summary: A 32-year-old Iranian asylum seeker, who was later identified as the perpetrator, took 15 passengers hostage on a train in the Vaud canton of Switzerland, brandishing an axe and forcing the conductor to move them to a separate carriage. After a four-hour standoff, police launched a raid, using diversionary explosives, and the perpetrator was fatally shot by an officer who was protecting the hostages. The hostages were safely released and reunited with their families.

head: RUAG verso un cambio di rotta
summary: The Swiss Federal Council is considering a change in the legal structure of the RUAG MRO, a defense industry company, due to its current form as a private limited company no longer meeting modern needs. The council has nominated Jürg Rötheli as the new chairman of the board, indicating a strategic shift to address pressing geopolitical and management challenges. An investigation by the Federal Finance Control Authority found inconsistencies in RUAG's business dealings, including the sale of Leopard 1 tanks, leading the council to explore alternative legal forms, including a possible return to a public department.

head: Nuovi raid sul Libano, morti anche due operatori dell’ONU
summary: Israeli airstrikes on Lebanon have killed at least 569 people, including six civilians and two UN staff members, with the death toll rising to 569, and 27,000 people displaced, as the conflict between Israel and Hezbollah continues, with Israel vowing to continue its attacks but ruling out a ground invasion.

head: Il bel tempo e la curiosità lanciano al meglio i Mondiali
summary: The 2023 World Championships in Zurich, Switzerland, kicked off with good weather and a large crowd, featuring a thrilling handbike mixed relay event won by France, while Swiss Cycling announced plans to establish a professional women's cycling team by 2025.

head: Maltempo, parlano cittadini e autorità
summary: Two months after devastating floods and landslides hit the Mesolcina and Vallemaggia regions in Switzerland, local residents and authorities are determined to find solutions to protect the areas from future natural disasters, with plans to implement new flood control measures and rebuild damaged infrastructure.

head: A Monaco piazze colme contro AfD, proteste interrotte
summary: Tens of thousands of people gathered in cities across Germany on Sunday to protest against the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party, with many demonstrations being interrupted due to overcrowding and concerns over public safety. The protests were sparked by revelations of a secret meeting between AfD members and far-right extremists, who discussed a plan to forcibly expel millions of foreigners and non-assimilated citizens from the country.

head: USA: Johnson rimane speaker, ma è stata dura
summary: Mike Johnson was re-elected as the Speaker of the US House of Representatives after a difficult first vote, in which he initially fell short of the quorum, but eventually secured the position with 218 votes against 215 after convincing two Republican lawmakers to change their vote.

head: Ucraina, viaggio nei punti di soccorso segreti lungo il fronte
summary: In Ukraine, a secret aid station near the front line provides emergency care to soldiers injured in the ongoing war, with a team of five people working tirelessly to stabilize patients and prepare them for transport to hospitals, amidst a war that has resulted in an estimated 60-80,000 deaths and over a million casualties.

head: Le due facce del turismo
summary: The Swiss tourism industry is expected to see a 12% increase in overnight stays this summer, but some regions are concerned about the impact of excessive tourism on local populations, leading to measures such as entrance fees and dynamic pricing to limit visitor numbers.

head: Sì all’abolizione del valore locativo e alla legge sull’identità elettronica
Cresce la pressione su Mosca, ma restano dubbi sulle sanzioni

head: Emergency: “A Gaza valichi chiusi, aiuti bloccati, bambini malnutriti”
summary: The situation in Gaza is deteriorating due to the closure of border crossings and the lack of aid, with 80% of the population living in temporary accommodations and 4.5% of children suffering from severe or moderate malnutrition.

head: L’addio di Cirillo e il margine di miglioramento per la Posta
summary: The CEO of the Swiss postal service, Roberto Cirillo, has resigned, leaving behind a mixed legacy of improvements and challenges, with some politicians expressing concerns about the communication and impact of recent transformations on employees and the public.

head: Monaco, 200’000 in piazza contro le autorità iraniane
summary: Approximately 200,000 people gathered in Munich, Germany, to protest against the Iranian government, calling for the downfall of the Islamic Republic, following a violent crackdown on protests in December. The demonstration was organized by a non-profit group and coincided with a security conference, where Iranian opposition leader Reza Pahlavi urged US President Donald Trump to intervene and help the Iranian people "bury" the current regime. Meanwhile, new nuclear talks between the US and Iran are set to take place in Geneva next week.

head: In Ticino l’antisemitismo è soprattutto online
summary: In Ticino, Switzerland, there have been no reported offline cases of antisemitism this year, but a one-month online monitoring revealed 27 episodes, which is a lower trend compared to the national increase in antisemitism cases after October 7, 2023.

head: Ucraina e Russia si bombardano a vicenda. Kiev usa gli Storm Shadow
summary: Ukraine and Russia have engaged in a series of retaliatory airstrikes, with Ukraine launching a large-scale combined air and missile attack on a Russian chemical plant in Bryansk, and Russia responding with airstrikes on Ukrainian cities, including Kiev, resulting in civilian casualties and damage.

head: Haiti in mano alle bande armate
summary: Haiti's Prime Minister Ariel Henry has resigned, paving the way for a transition period amidst a severe humanitarian crisis, with armed gangs controlling over 80% of the capital and the country's political and economic systems in chaos.

head: Asilanti al Seghezzone, De Rosa: “Escludo che ci saranno i casi problematici”
summary: A temporary asylum seeker center in Giubiasco, Switzerland will accommodate up to 88 people in prefabricated modules and is expected to be operational by the end of June, with a planned duration of four years before a permanent location is found.

head: UDC: no agli accordi con l’UE, “minacciano la sovranità svizzera”
summary: The Swiss Democratic Centre party has rejected the country's agreements with the European Union, citing concerns that they threaten Switzerland's sovereignty, independence, and democratic rights, and potentially putting the country's prosperity at risk.

head: Angelina Jolie visita il valico di Rafah
summary: Actress Angelina Jolie visited the Rafah border crossing in Egypt to show her support for the people of Gaza, a Palestinian territory devastated by two years of war, and to personally observe the conditions of injured Palestinians and the transportation of humanitarian aid.

head: Canone a 300 franchi, chi è pro e chi è contro
summary: The Swiss government has proposed reducing the annual fee for public broadcasting from 335 to 300 francs, but a coalition of left-wing parties, unions, and cultural organizations has expressed strong opposition, warning of severe consequences for the country's media landscape and public service.

head: Steckborn, larga maggioranza a favore del centro d’asilo
summary: The residents of Steckborn, a small Swiss town, have overwhelmingly approved the maintenance of a center for asylum seekers, rejecting a proposal by a local group to close the facility due to concerns over safety and security issues.

head: Sudan, la guerra dimenticata
summary: The ongoing civil war in Sudan, which has lasted nearly three years, has led to a severe humanitarian crisis, with an estimated 150,000 deaths and over 10 million displaced people, half of whom are children. The conflict between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces has caused widespread destruction, famine, and violence, with the international community struggling to provide adequate aid.

head: Ucraina, quando anche i civili si preparano a combattere
summary: In Ukraine, a training center is preparing civilians to defend themselves against potential Russian attacks by teaching them basic military skills, such as disarming mines, using firearms, and operating drones, in a 7-week course that is voluntary and open to people of all ages and professions.

head: Richiedenti problematici: i sindaci della regione non ci stanno
summary: The Swiss government plans to create a separate area within the Pasture asylum center for individuals considered problematic, who have exhibited violent or threatening behavior, with the goal of implementing a pilot project to improve safety and tranquility within the center.

head: Il martin pescatore è l’uccello dell’anno 2026
summary: The martin pescatore, a small bird with a vibrant plumage, has been elected "Bird of the Year 2026" by BirdLife Svizzera, despite being a species at risk of extinction due to habitat loss and degradation in Switzerland.

head: La guerra a Gaza provoca una frattura nel PS
L’espansione delle strade non convince
summary: Users on the online platform "dialogo" debated the best solution to combat traffic congestion, with 78% favoring a reduction in traffic rather than expanding the road network, citing concerns about increased traffic and environmental impact.

head: La propaganda dello Stato islamico per i minori
summary: The Islamic State is using online gaming platforms, social media, and forums to indoctrinate children with violent and extremist ideologies, often through simulations of past or potential future terrorist attacks.

head: “L’obiettivo sarà di condividere una visione positiva del Ticino”
summary: Norman Gobbi has been elected as the new president of the Government of Ticino, Switzerland, succeeding Christian Vitta, and has outlined his priorities to promote a positive vision of the region, foster a stronger connection between citizens and institutions, and implement measures to address the canton's financial challenges.

head: L’MPS a Lugano spera in dieci schede in più
summary: The Movimento per il socialismo (MPS) is running in the municipal elections in Lugano and Bellinzona, aiming to increase their presence in the city councils, with a focus on defending public schools, elderly homes, and social rights, and potentially entering the Lugano city council for the first time.

head: Molestie sessuali, strade e mezzi pubblici i luoghi “caldi”
summary: In Switzerland, data from cities Berna and Zurigo shows that most sexual harassment occurs on streets or public transportation, prompting campaigns to encourage citizens to report incidents and show "civic courage" to support victims.

head: Gaza: Croce Rossa, aiuti in distribuzione
summary: Humanitarian aid, including food, medicine, and medical equipment, has begun to be distributed to vulnerable populations in Gaza, after Israel gave the green light for aid trucks to enter the enclave, following 11 weeks of blockade that led to the deaths of 29 children and elderly people due to starvation in the past two days.

head: Il futuro incerto dei profughi siriani in Germania
summary: A month after the fall of the Assad regime, German politicians are debating whether to allow Syrian refugees to return to their homeland for a "reconnaissance" visit without losing their refugee status, as the future of nearly one million Syrians living in Germany remains uncertain.

head: Il vertice dell’UDC boccia la 13esima AVS
summary: The Swiss UDC party has recommended rejecting a proposed 13th pension supplement, with 301 delegates voting in favor of rejection, while the party's base and some sections appear less opposed to the idea.

head: Patto migrazione UE, le reazioni svizzere
summary: The European Union's migration agreement has sparked mixed reactions in Switzerland, with the federal counselor Elisabeth Baume-Schneider welcoming the accord as a step towards greater cooperation, while the Swiss Refugee Aid Organization expresses concerns about a potential tightening of European asylum policies.

head: Un autunno ricco di castagne
summary: In Ticino, Switzerland, the chestnut harvest is abundant and the chestnut moth population is under control, but the region's wild chestnut forests, which are important for protection, are threatened by drought and overgrazing by ungulates.

head: Richiedenti l’asilo, accoglienza a distanza
summary: In Albania, a pilot project is underway to manage migration, where migrants arriving from the sea will be diverted to registration and reception centers, with the first control taking place in Albania before they proceed to Italy, sparking concerns about the involvement of local population and the practical and ethical implications of distant asylum processing.

head: Profitti record per le banche svizzere nel 2023
summary: Swiss banks reported record profits and increased employment in 2023, with a historic result attributed to the UBS-Credit Suisse merger, and a strong growth in the financial sector.

head: Costi della salute, l’UDC ticinese presenta 6 mozioni
summary: The UDC party in the Swiss canton of Ticino has presented six motions to address the high healthcare costs in the region, arguing that the canton has not done enough to contain expenses, which are the highest in Switzerland.

head: Mezza Europa flagellata dal maltempo
summary: Heavy rainfall and flooding caused by the storm Boris have resulted in numerous deaths and left thousands of people homeless in central and eastern Europe, with widespread damage and power outages reported in several countries.

head: Come cambia la gestione delle epidemie
summary: The Swiss Federal Council has approved a revised law on epidemics, which clarifies the division of responsibilities between the federal government and cantons in managing public health crises, including the preparation and implementation of pandemic plans, without introducing a mandatory vaccination requirement.

head: Exit poll, Lukashenko verso il settimo mandato con l’87,6% dei voti
summary: Bielorussian President Alexander Lukashenko has won a seventh term in office with 87.6% of the vote, according to exit polls, in an election that international observers have deemed neither free nor fair due to the repression of opposition figures and independent media.

head: Gli Stati Uniti hanno lanciato 38’000 pasti su Gaza
summary: The United States has conducted its first airdrop of aid to the population in the Gaza Strip, dropping 38,000 meals and medications from three American C-130 aircraft, with more operations planned in the coming days.

head: El Doraltdorf
summary: Dozens of Ticinese residents commute daily to Altdorf in Canton Uri, Switzerland, attracted by higher salaries, a healthier work culture, and better work-life balance, thanks to the Alptransit rail project that connects the region to the rest of Switzerland.

head: Ospedale cantonale dei Grigioni in rosso
summary: The Canton Hospital of the Grisons in Switzerland reported a loss of 339,000 francs in 2024 due to financial burdens, including inflation and unadjusted tariffs, despite having a profitable operational result of 543.4 million francs.

head: UBS chiude 85 filiali “doppie” entro marzo 2025
summary: UBS plans to consolidate 85 duplicate branches by March 2025 and expects to have around 190 remaining branches by the end of 2026, following the integration of Credit Suisse.

head: Cicitt: il sapore antico delle Valli del Locarnese
summary: In the Swiss region of Vallemaggia, a traditional autumnal sausage called Cicitt is prepared using the meat of old, often toothless or barren, goats. The sausage has a rich history dating back to the early 20th century and is a symbol of the region's agricultural heritage. The production of Cicitt is a labor of love that involves a family recipe passed down through generations, and the sausage is typically cooked over an open flame. However, the traditional practice of raising goats in the region is facing challenges, including the lack of young people willing to take over the profession and the increasing restrictions on grazing.

head: “Facciamo ciò che possiamo con i mezzi che abbiamo”
summary: Switzerland is increasingly confronted with terrorism and organized crime, but the justice system often lacks the necessary tools to effectively combat these threats, according to outgoing Federal Police Director Nicoletta Della Valle, who highlights the risks of jihadism and the mafia's presence in the country.

head: Morti a Gaza: “Per il 70% donne e bambini”
summary: A report by the United Nations Office for the High Commissioner for Human Rights states that approximately 70% of the people killed in Gaza over six months due to Israeli attacks, bombings, and other hostile actions were civilians, including women and children, indicating a systematic violation of fundamental principles of international humanitarian law.

head: La Russia apre un nuovo fronte a nord di Kharkiv
summary: Russian troops have opened a new front in Ukraine, crossing the border from the Belgorod region into Kharkiv, and advancing about a kilometer towards Vovchansk, with Ukrainian forces reportedly resisting and civilians being evacuated from the area.

head: Quando le piazze di tiro sono troppo rumorose
summary: Residents in Switzerland are protesting against the increasing noise from military firing ranges, citing health concerns and disruptions to daily life. The government has been urged to update noise-reducing measures, but the military has pushed back, citing the need for realistic and credible military training, and the potential costs of implementing new noise-reducing measures.

head: La rivoluzione del carrello della spesa
summary: The introduction of self-service supermarkets in Switzerland in the 1940s revolutionized the way people shopped, leading to increased convenience, abundance, and changes in societal attitudes towards food and consumption.

head: Social dai 16 anni, d’accordo la maggioranza della popolazione
summary: A majority of the Swiss population, with 78% in agreement, supports limiting access to social media platforms such as TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram to individuals aged 16 and above.

head: Salari, fra la Svizzera e... il Ticino il divario cresce ancora
summary: In Switzerland, the median monthly gross salary for a full-time job was 6,788 francs in 2022, but in the canton of Ticino it was only 5,590 francs, resulting in a growing salary gap between the two regions.

head: Per una scuola Steiner che chiude, ce ne è una che va bene
summary: A Steiner school in Origlio, Switzerland is closing, but another school in Minusio is experiencing an increase in enrollment, with over 166 students and 122 families choosing to continue their education there, in contrast to a national trend of declining interest in Steiner schools, which have seen a decrease from over 6,300 students in 2013 to around 5,200 this year.

head: Nuovo avvistamento dell’orso nei Grigioni
summary: A bear has been spotted in the Swiss canton of Grisons, with authorities confirming its presence after a photo trap captured the animal two days prior, following earlier sightings in May.

head: Successione Amherd, la corsa degli “altri” candidati
summary: Two independent candidates, an entrepreneur from Fribourg and a spokesperson for the Geneva police, have announced their bids for the Swiss Federal Council, citing their personal and professional experience as key qualifications, despite the fact that no independent candidate has ever been elected to the position since 1848.

head: Presidenziali dall’esito scontato in Egitto
summary: Egyptians are voting in a presidential election that is widely expected to result in the re-election of incumbent President Abdel Fatah al Sissi, who faces little opposition from three nominal rivals.

head: Una città privata in un paradiso tropicale
Patrouille Suisse: da non mantenere nella forma attuale
summary: Swiss lawmakers have rejected a motion to maintain the country's aerobatic squadron, Patrouille Suisse, in its current form due to the high costs associated with maintaining the outdated F-5 Tiger jets used by the team.

head: Guardie di custodia: “privilegiare i cittadini svizzeri”
summary: Swiss government officials, including Norman Gobbi, prefer to hire local citizens as prison guards, citing the importance of prioritizing Swiss citizenship in the selection process, while union representatives propose expanding the recruitment pool to include residents with a C permit.

head: Camere federali al lavoro
Ucraini e integrazione, “misure efficaci”
summary: Two years after the start of the Russia-Ukraine war, the situation of refugees in Switzerland remains uncertain, with approximately 86,000 people having sought protection status S, but the integration measures are considered effective, with a positive employment rate of around 22% among Ukrainian refugees, and efforts being made to improve language skills and provide childcare options.

head: Baume-Schneider, “non una fuga ma un’opportunità”
summary: Elisabeth Baume-Schneider, a Swiss federal counselor, has taken on the responsibility of the Federal Department of the Interior, leaving the Department of Justice and Police after one year, citing it as an opportunity to utilize her skills in healthcare, social affairs, and culture.

head: Ebrei e palestinesi, l’esempio della convivenza pacifica
summary: Residents of the village of Neve Shalom/Wahdi al Salam, a community of 300 people where Israelis and Palestinians live together, share their model of peaceful coexistence, emphasizing the importance of dialogue, respect, and education in promoting peace between Israelis and Palestinians.

head: Fortezza Europa: dentro i movimenti identitari
summary: Extremist right-wing groups in Europe are organizing around the concept of "remigration," which involves the deportation of migrants from the continent to preserve what they consider "the ethnic and cultural identity of the continent." These groups, known as "identitarians," are active in various European countries, including Switzerland, and are using social media to promote their message and organize events, such as the "Remigration Summit 2025" in Italy, which drew attention for its calls for the deportation of migrants and the creation of a "fortress Europe."

head: Dopo le polemiche riprendono i finanziamenti all’UNRWA
summary: Canada and Sweden have announced plans to resume financial aid to the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees (UNRWA) after suspending it due to allegations of UNRWA employees' involvement in a Hamas attack, with the agency agreeing to increased oversight and audits.

head: “Democrazia diretta sempre più limitata”
summary: A Swiss constitutional expert, Andreas Kley, notes that the country's direct democracy is often limited in practice, citing examples where popular initiatives have been partially or completely ignored by the government, including a 2014 initiative on mass immigration and a 1994 initiative on Alpine transportation. Kley argues that the government tends to disregard initiatives that it finds inconvenient or damaging, and that this undermines the principles of direct democracy and the Swiss Constitution.

head: Siriani in Svizzera, “ogni caso venga valutato singolarmente”
summary: The Swiss government has temporarily suspended asylum procedures for Syrians, citing the need for clarity on the situation in Syria after the fall of the Assad regime, and plans to individually assess each case.

head: Il fronte libanese, pesanti bombardamenti isralieani
summary: The Israeli military has continued to launch heavy bombardments in southern and eastern Lebanon, prompting the Lebanese defense forces to advise civilians to evacuate areas associated with the Hezbollah organization, which Israel has accused of transforming the region into a combat zone.

head: “C’è indivualismo, per il futuro non sono ottimista”
summary: Noémie Roten, the driving force behind a Swiss initiative for mandatory community service, is not disappointed by the initiative's rejection, as she believes it sparked important discussions on issues such as national cohesion, equality, and military preparedness.

head: I miliardi che mancano nel Green
summary: Europe's efforts to transition to a carbon-neutral economy by 2050 are hindered by a lack of investment, with the European Union investing significantly less than the US and China, which have invested $890 billion and $370 billion respectively in the past year, highlighting the need for massive investment to achieve the goal of reducing carbon emissions.

head: La crisi dell’esercito svizzero
summary: The Swiss army is facing significant challenges in defending the country, including a shortage of personnel, outdated equipment, and financial scandals, which have raised concerns about its ability to respond to modern threats.

head: Picconate dell’UDC sulla politica migratoria: “Un caos”
summary: The Swiss People's Party (UDC) has criticized the government's immigration policies, labeling them as "chaotic," and called for stricter border controls and a stronger defense.

head: Il rame di Panama
summary: Panama, a country with zero net emissions, is seeking to eliminate its lucrative mining industry, particularly the copper mining sector, which has been a major contributor to its economy but also poses significant environmental concerns.

head: Sanità: diplomi stranieri maggiormente accettati
summary: The number of foreign diplomas recognized in Switzerland for various healthcare professions, including nurses and physical therapists, has been increasing significantly, with over 51,000 diplomas recognized between 2013 and 2024, and more than 5,800 in 2024 alone.

head: Khan Yunis, almeno 90 morti. Il raid forse fallito.
summary: At least 90 people have been killed and over 300 injured in an Israeli airstrike on a humanitarian zone in Gaza, with the target believed to be the Hamas military commander Mohammed Deif, although his status is unclear.

head: Ospedale di Samedan, primo “no” alla fusione con Coira
summary: The town of La Punt Chamues-ch in Switzerland has rejected a proposal to merge the local hospital with the cantonal hospital in Chur, with 45 residents voting against the plan, making it the first of eleven towns in the region to do so.

head: In difesa dell’umanità
summary: Amnesty International's annual report highlights both positive developments and areas of concern regarding human rights in Switzerland, including the establishment of the Swiss Institution for Human Rights and the need for improvements in refugee family reunification and freedom of assembly.

head: I molluschi, questi sconosciuti
summary: In Switzerland, over 40% of mollusks are threatened with extinction, but they play a crucial role in soil formation. The Swiss organization Pro Natura has designated the fascinate snail as the "animal of the year 2025" to raise awareness about the importance of decomposers, which include mollusks, in maintaining soil fertility and ecosystem balance.

head: Lo Stretto di Hormuz: cos’è ma soprattutto perché è così importante
summary: The Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway separating the Arabian Peninsula from Iran, has seen a significant reduction in maritime traffic due to Iran's response to US and Israeli airstrikes, with over 150 oil tankers blocked or threatened, potentially disrupting global trade and leading to a 7% increase in oil prices and a 32% increase in European gas prices.

head: La fuga di Assad finisce a Mosca
Swisscom sconta Vodafone, ma aumenta i dividendi
summary: Swisscom, the Swiss telecommunications leader, reported a 17.6% decline in net profit to 1.27 billion Swiss francs due to integration costs from its acquisition of Vodafone Italy, but increased dividends for shareholders.

head: Sparatoria in una scuola USA, sospettata una 15enne
summary: A 15-year-old student, identified as Natalie Rupnow, is suspected of fatally shooting a teacher and a classmate at the Abundant Life Christian School in Madison, Wisconsin, before allegedly taking her own life.

head: Statuto S, servono 185 milioni in più
summary: The Swiss government has requested an additional 302 million Swiss francs from parliament to cover expenses related to the integration of Ukrainian refugees, including 185 million for social assistance and 86 million for a European research program.

head: Guerra in Ucraina: tra paura, sgomento e speranza
summary: Four years after the start of the Russian invasion of Ukraine, a Ukrainian woman named Tetyana Vaccaro Zakharchenko, who has lived in Switzerland for over 20 years, shares her personal experience of the war and her efforts to help Ukrainian refugees, highlighting the ongoing fears, confusion, and hope for an end to the conflict.

head: Quando Giulio Cesare negò il mare agli Elvezi
summary: A photographic exhibition at the Roman Museum in Avenches, Switzerland, tells the story of the failed migration of the Celtic Elvezi people, who attempted to reach the Atlantic Ocean in the 1st century AD, but were blocked by Julius Caesar, leading to a significant turning point in the conquest of Gaul.

head: Blatten, via libera all’intervento dell’esercito
summary: A team of approximately 20 military personnel has begun removing debris and wood from a lake formed in the Blatten area after a glacier collapse, to prevent water stagnation and potential flooding.

head: La sessione autunnale è terminata
summary: The Swiss federal parliament's autumn session has concluded with key issues, including individual taxation, rental income, and the military budget, remaining unresolved.

head: Coira ha inaugurato la stanza del consumo
summary: The city of Coira in Switzerland has inaugurated a controlled consumption room for individuals struggling with addiction, aiming to improve their health, quality of life, and safety in public spaces, while also reducing the presence of open drug scenes in the city.

head: Viola Amherd, promozione della pace al centro dei colloqui
summary: Swiss President Viola Amherd met with Italian President Sergio Mattarella and Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni in Rome to discuss various topics, including the promotion of peace, the fight against child abuse in the Catholic Church, and cooperation on issues such as transportation and migration.

head: Per gli specialisti, meno medici non vuol dire meno costi
summary: In the Swiss canton of Ticino, a new regulation limiting the number of new doctors in certain specialties has been implemented to control healthcare costs, but specialists are concerned that this approach may compromise the quality of healthcare.

head: Sessa: protesta per la scuola
summary: Residents of the Sessa neighborhood in Tresa are protesting a proposed school reform that would consolidate the first cycle of students in Sessa and transfer the second cycle to Croglio, citing concerns over increased travel times and the potential closure of the Sessa school.

head: Netanyahu operato di ernia, interim per Levin
summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is undergoing surgery for an inguinal hernia and will be temporarily replaced by Vice Premier and Justice Minister Zariv Levin. Meanwhile, the Israeli military has struck a Jihad Islamic command center in Gaza, and Hamas has not yet decided to send a delegation for new peace talks, citing that positions are still too far apart. In other news, the Jordanian government has announced the arrest of "troublemakers" in a refugee camp, and a new law in Israel will block government funding for ultra-orthodox students who avoid military service.

head: “Biden ha cacciato 2,8 milioni di migranti, più di Trump”
summary: President Joe Biden's administration has deported more migrants than former President Donald Trump's in their first two years, with 2.8 million migrants expelled under Biden compared to 2 million under Trump.

head: Grigioni ed extra muros del Gran Consiglio: avanti Vals
summary: The Conferenza dei presidenti (CP) of the Rhaeto-Romance Parliament has chosen Vals as the preferred location for an extra-mural session of the Gran Consiglio in 2027, ahead of other candidates including the Moesa region, Scuol, and St-Moritz.

head: Il Vallese, la rete Polycom che fa cilecca e i dubbi a Berna
summary: A recent snowstorm in the Swiss valleys of Saas and Zermatt caused a critical failure of the Polycom radio network, which is used by emergency services, leaving them without communication for 24 hours. This incident has raised concerns and will be discussed in Parliament, highlighting issues with the network's reliability and maintenance, as well as plans to replace it with a new system using 3GPP technology by 2035.

head: Accordi con l’UE, i punti dolenti secondo il Governo ticinese
summary: The Swiss Ticino government has submitted a position to the federal council requesting modifications to the EU agreement package, specifically regarding the safeguard clause and referendum requirements, citing concerns that the current proposal may negatively impact the region.

head: La scia di Starlink sulla Svizzera
summary: A Starlink satellite re-entered the Earth's atmosphere over Switzerland, with reports of a bright trail visible in the sky in various cities in Germany and Switzerland.

head: Migranti, chiude il centro di Paradiso
summary: A migrant center in Paradiso, Switzerland is being temporarily relocated to a hotel due to structural issues with the building, which will be uninhabitable after December 31, 2024, and requires costly repairs to extend its lease beyond 2024.

head: Conflitto in Medio Oriente, gli Stati Europei si espongono a metà
summary: European countries have condemned Iran's attacks on Gulf monarchies, but have been less decisive in criticizing the US and Israel for violating international law, with some analysts suggesting that this is due to fear of being abandoned by the US in the event of a prolonged conflict in Ukraine.

head: Il porto temporaneo a Gaza piace, ma non a tutti
summary: US President Joe Biden has proposed a temporary port in Gaza to deliver humanitarian aid, but the idea has raised concerns from the United Nations, which prefers a land-based solution, while the European Union has announced the opening of its first maritime corridor to provide aid to the Gaza population.

head: UE-Egitto, firmata l’intesa su migranti ed energia
summary: The European Union and Egypt have signed a strategic partnership agreement worth 7.4 billion euros over three years, focusing on energy and migration, with Egypt set to receive 5 billion euros in loans, 1.8 billion euros in investments, and 600 million euros in aid for migration-related programs.

head: “L’età di Trump e Biden un problema? C’è di peggio”
Gaza: Biden ai ferri corti con Netanyahu
summary: US President Joe Biden and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu are at odds over Israel's potential large-scale operation in the Gaza Strip city of Rafah, with Biden warning that such an action would not guarantee the defeat of Hamas and Netanyahu responding that Israel will proceed with or without US support.

head: La canicola non molla
summary: A severe heatwave warning has been extended in parts of Switzerland, including Ticino and the Basso Moesano, with temperatures expected to reach up to 34 degrees Celsius and authorities advising residents to take precautions to avoid heat-related illnesses.

head: Davos, due fermi per l’aggressione a un giovane ebreo
summary: Two asylum seekers, a 24-year-old and a 29-year-old, have been arrested in Davos, Switzerland, for allegedly attacking a 19-year-old Jewish tourist from the UK, and are also suspected of committing other crimes, including two burglaries, on the same night.

head: Sudafrica, il partito che fu di Mandela non governerà più solo
summary: The African National Congress, the historic party led by Nelson Mandela that ended apartheid in South Africa, has lost its absolute majority in the parliamentary elections, forcing the formation of a coalition government with uncertain partners.

head: La FINMA boccia ancora il piano di emergenza di Postfinance
summary: The Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) has evaluated the emergency plans of major Swiss banks, finding that Postfinance's plan still has significant gaps, while the Zurich Cantonal Bank's plan was deemed feasible, and UBS has not yet been evaluated due to its ongoing integration with Credit Suisse.

head: Il vetro svizzero si ricicla all’estero
summary: In Switzerland, a country with one of the highest glass recycling rates in the world, most of the collected glass is exported for recycling, with over 80% of it being sent abroad since the closure of the last glass factory in June 2024.

head: Eccesso di legittima difesa, condannato un canapaio
summary: A Swiss farmer was sentenced to 46 months in prison for using excessive force in self-defense when he shot at intruders who had attacked him on his property in 2016.

head: Parsi: “Trump ascolta solo Israele”
summary: Italian professor Vittorio Emanuele Parsi argues that the US administration under Trump is ignoring the concerns of its Arab allies and the European Union, prioritizing Israel's interests, and that this approach may lead to a lesson for Iran that those with nuclear capabilities can maintain power, while those without risk falling, similar to the cases of North Korea and Iraq under Saddam Hussein.

head: La piscina di Grono è in dirittura d’arrivo
summary: The municipality of Grono in Switzerland has announced the approval process for a new swimming pool project, which is expected to cost around 5 million francs, and will be put to a public vote on May 18.

head: Coira aumenta gli scranni dei municipali
summary: The city council of Chur, Switzerland, has approved a motion to increase the number of municipal members from 3 to 5 to better represent the population, despite concerns from the current administration that this would increase costs and workload.

head: Sudafrica, il partito che fu di Mandela non governerà più solo
summary: The African National Congress, the historic party led by Nelson Mandela that ended apartheid in South Africa, has lost its absolute majority in the parliamentary elections, with its vote share dropping to around 40%, potentially leading to a coalition government.

head: Caso Gobbi ancora senza risposte
summary: The government of the Swiss canton of Ticino has refused to provide answers to three parliamentary questions regarding the "Gobbi case", a road accident involving a high-ranking official, citing an ongoing investigation and the need to await the outcome of a related criminal procedure.

head: Vitalizi limitati per gli ex consiglieri di Stato grigionesi
summary: The Swiss cantonal parliament of Grisons has accepted a government proposal to limit lifetime pensions for former state counselors to three years, rejecting a proposal to abolish them entirely and paving the way for a possible public vote on the issue.

head: #Svizzerando e i quadri in prestito

Today, approximately 300 lynx live in Switzerland, with two subpopulations in the Alps and Jura mountains showing signs of genetic exchange. head: Migranti, il telefonino ora può dire da dove arrivano
summary: In Switzerland, a three-month pilot project has begun in Chiasso and Basel, allowing authorities to access and analyze the electronic devices of asylum seekers to determine their origin, age, and travel history, sparking controversy among NGOs who argue it infringes on their right to privacy.

head: La Cavia ritorna con tante nuove avventure
summary: The Italian television program "La Cavia" returns for its third season, focusing on the theme of freedom, with host Valerio Thoeny exploring various aspects of it through four central topics: travel, courage, the body, and presence, and incorporating digital content and audience participation.

head: L’invecchiamento della Cina fa gola

head: La Germania rimpatria gli afghani, l’ONU: “Fermatevi”
summary: The German government has forcibly repatriated 81 Afghan nationals with criminal convictions to Afghanistan, sparking criticism from the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights and Amnesty International, who argue that these individuals are at risk of persecution.

summary: Researchers in Switzerland have found high levels of the insecticide fipronil in rivers and streams, despite its ban in agriculture since 2013, with the substance contaminating waterways through its use in pet products for dogs and cats.

summary: Swiss beverage producers who signed the Milan Declaration last year to reduce sugar content in their products by 10% by 2024 have made limited progress, with some brands still containing high levels of sugar, such as Fanta, which has double the sugar content in Switzerland compared to the UK.

head: Entomologia urbana: quante sfide!

summary: Heavy snowfall and freezing temperatures caused widespread disruptions in the UK and the US, with many flights cancelled, roads closed, and emergency declarations issued in several states.

head: Un abitante della Svizzera su otto ha almeno una fattura non pagata
summary: In Switzerland, approximately 40.9% of the population lived in a household with at least one unpaid bill or debt in 2022, with 12.1% having at least one unpaid bill and 37.6% having at least one type of credit. The most common types of unpaid bills were taxes and health insurance premiums, while the most common types of credit were used to finance mortgages, home improvements, and daily expenses.

head: Israele colpisce scuola UNRWA nella Striscia di Gaza
summary: The Israeli military conducted an airstrike on a UNRWA school in the Gaza Strip, killing at least 27 people and injuring many others, as they targeted Hamas militants who were allegedly inside the building.

head: Il ritorno al potere di Trump
In Giordania dove i ragazzi boicottano Israele

head: Detenuti sessuali in carcere, ma non isolati: funziona
summary: Five years after the abolition of separate sections for sex offenders in Swiss prisons, the approach has been deemed successful, with sex offenders being integrated into the general prison population and showing improved behavior and rehabilitation prospects.

head: UE: via libera a dazi sulle auto elettriche cinesi
summary: The European Commission has received the necessary support from EU member states to impose tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles, despite divisions among member countries, and will proceed with the measure while continuing negotiations with China for a WTO-compliant solution.

head: Blatten, il villaggio sarà ricostruito entro cinque anni
summary: The village of Blatten in Switzerland will be rebuilt within three to five years after a devastating landslide in May, with plans to relocate the community to the Eisten, Weissenried, and historic center areas, featuring new roads, a town square, and a church.
